instructions: Cut the steak into 4 even cutlets. Place one between two sheets of plastic wrap and pound it with a meat mallet or the bottom of a heavy pan until it's about 1/4 inch thick. Do the rest the same way.
Set up three shallow dishes. In the first, mix the flour, 1 tsp of the salt and the black pepper. In the second, beat the eggs with the garlic, minced. Put the breadcrumbs in the third.
Coat each cutlet in the flour, then the egg, then press it into the breadcrumbs on both sides. Transfer the cutlets to a rack or a plate and leave them for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, make the salad. Tear the lettuce into a large bowl. Add the tomatoes cut into wedges and half the red onion, thinly sliced. Leave the salad undressed for now.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat, until a pinch of breadcrumbs sizzles right away. The oil should be about 1/2 inch deep.
Lay 2 cutlets in the pan. Fry for 2 to 3 minutes, until the underside is deep golden. Flip them and fry the other side for 2 to 3 minutes. Don't crowd the pan.
Transfer the cutlets to a paper towel lined plate, then fry the other 2 the same way. Sprinkle the cutlets with the remaining 1/2 tsp salt while they're hot.
Juice one of the limes over the salad, add the olive oil and toss. Cut the other lime into wedges.
Taste the salad. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve the milanesas with the lime wedges and the salad.
method_notes: Both versions agree on thin top round, a flour, egg and breadcrumb coating, and a shallow fry of about 3 minutes a side. The lead adds flour and garlic in the egg, while the second version skips the flour and uses only egg and crumbs. This version follows the lead, adds a simple lime salad, and pounds the cutlets to 1/4 inch so each side needs only 2 to 3 minutes.
